source_book: NCERT Class 11 Ch.5 Laws of Motion — table-of-contents reference only (Newton's third law is its own section, immediately after the second law, before constraint/pulley problems); teaching authored from first principles. The atomic idea: forces come in pairs — when body 1 pushes body 2, body 2 simultaneously pushes body 1 with EQUAL magnitude and OPPOSITE direction, and because the two forces act on DIFFERENT bodies they never cancel. Does NOT cover how much a force accelerates a body (newton_second_law, used here only as the a = F/m read-off), drawing complete force diagrams (free_body_diagram), friction or inclines (block_on_incline), string-coupled bodies (connected_bodies), or momentum conservation. Engine: the shared newtons_laws_body field_3d scenario (docs/NEWTONS_LAWS_BODY_ENGINE_SPEC.md) — a flat frictionless surface (theta_deg = 0, mu = 0 throughout) carrying two independent bodies (no pulley), with action_reaction.engaged mirroring the driver body's applied force onto its partner every frame. All four states are expressible with the engine's existing config surface; ENGINE GAP: none.

real_world_anchor.primary: Two people on smooth-rolling chairs push off each other's palms — both roll away, and the lighter person always rolls away faster, no matter who did the pushing: the push you give is exactly the push you get back.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A rocket in empty space hurls exhaust gas backward, and the gas pushes the rocket forward with the same force — nothing external to push against is needed.

aha_moment.statement: Equal-and-opposite forces never cancel — they never act on the same body.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: On block one's own diagram, mg and N — which DO share this body — visibly cancel, while F₁₂'s partner is nowhere in this diagram (it lives on block two, held as a dimmed ghost); F_net reads 30.00 N and block one accelerates away while the ghost holds its pose.

F_net.name: net force on the isolated body (STATE_3 only)
F_net.derived: F12 (no partner force acts on this same body)

acceleration_ratio_S2.formula: a_A / a_B = m2 / m (with m2 = 3*m, ratio = 1:3)

force_equality_check_S1_S2.formula: abs(F_applied_A) = abs(F_applied_B) at every instant, all masses

constraints: F12 = -F21 at every instant, engine-enforced by action_reaction.engaged (never hand-authored twice)
the two forces of a pair act on DIFFERENT bodies, so their sum is never evaluated as a single body's net force
each body's own acceleration is a = (its own net force) / (its own mass) -- independent of the partner body's mass
on m1's own diagram (STATE_3), mg and N cancel because BOTH act on m1 -- a balanced-force fact about ONE body, not a third-law pair
theta = 0 and mu_s = mu_k = 0 in every state (flat frictionless floor throughout; no incline, no pulley, no hanging body)
ghost bodies are never integrated and carry no readouts -- a ghost's position is fixed, decorative context only

every authored applied_force_N in every state (and the sandbox idle_auto_sweep/slider range) is >= 15 N, so raw arrow length (F * NLB_ARROW_SCALE = F * 0.030) is always >= 0.45, at least 1.5x NLB_ARROW_MIN_LEN (0.30)

STATE_1.title: One push, two forces: both bodies recoil symmetrically

scene_composition.text: Two equal blocks start together, side by side, at rest
Both arrows appear together -- same length, opposite direction
like two people on rolling chairs pushing off each other's palms

tts_sentences.text_en: Two blocks start together, side by side, at rest.
One block pushes off the other, and instantly both feel a force: one arrow points from block two onto block one, an identical arrow points the other way -- same length, opposite direction.
And both blocks recoil apart, together.

STATE_2.title: Unequal masses, equal forces: 1:3 masses, identical arrows, 3:1 accelerations

scene_composition.text: Two identical force arrows -- only the mass differs
m₂ carries three times the mass -- a reads exactly one third
drag the m₂ slider -- its recoil changes live, the arrow never does

tts_sentences.text_en: Same push, new masses -- block two now carries three times block one's mass.
Watch the two force arrows: exactly the same length, however unequal the blocks.
Yet block one shoots away fast while block two barely creeps, its acceleration exactly one third.
Drag block two's mass and watch that gap change live.

misconception_watch.belief: The bigger, stronger, or heavier one pushes harder -- the winner of a push exerts the greater force (planted by lived experience: the heavier person 'wins' every shoving match, so their force must be larger).
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Masses are 1:3, yet the two applied-force arrows are pixel-identical in length and the two force readouts read the same 30.0 N -- the ONLY unequal thing is the accelerations, 0.10 vs 0.033, exactly 3:1.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The forces are always equal -- mass decides who moves more, never who pushes more.

STATE_3.title: Why the pair never cancels: isolate m1's own diagram

scene_composition.text: Block one, alone -- watch its own three forces
mg and N cancel -- both act on this SAME block
F₁₂'s partner is on block two, not on this diagram
ΣF here is not zero -- block one accelerates

tts_sentences.text_en: Its weight pulls down, the surface pushes up -- equal, opposite, and they cancel, because both act on this same block.
The horizontal push has no such partner here; its partner acts on block two, not on this diagram.
So block one's net force is not zero, and it accelerates.

misconception_watch.belief: Equal and opposite forces cancel -- so if every action has an equal reaction, nothing should ever move.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: On block one's own diagram, mg and N -- which DO share this body -- cancel visibly, while F₁₂'s partner is nowhere in this diagram (it acts on the dimmed ghost, block two); F_net reads 30.00 N and block one accelerates.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Forces cancel only when they act on the SAME body -- a third-law pair never does.

STATE_4.title: Explore: any two masses, any push -- forces always equal, accelerations always m2:m1

scene_composition.text: Set both masses and the push -- watch the arrows and readouts respond live
drag m₂ huge -- arrows stay twins, its recoil dies; drag F -- both recoils scale together

tts_sentences.text_en: Your turn -- drag the masses and the push, and watch the two force arrows stay twins while the accelerations split by mass.
